newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Another businessman kidnapped in Philippines.
newsitem.headline: Another businessman kidnapped in Philippines.

text.p: Three men disguised as preachers on Tuesday kidnapped a Filipino-Chinese realtor in the second abduction of a businessman in the southern Philippines this week, police said.
Raymundo Tan had just got out of his car in Iligan city on Mindanao island when the men, wearing priests' robes, forced him back in at gunpoint and drove off.
Police said they wanted to question a driver Tan recently fired, adding they had no evidence to suggest a rebel group was involved.

Suspected Moslem guerrillas on Sunday kidnapped Japanese businessman Kenichi Takayama and three Filipinos from a beach resort on Sarangani island, 320 km (200 miles) southeast of Iligan. They shot dead another Filipino on the beach.
Soldiers rescued Takayama and the others on Monday after killing two of the kidnappers in a gun battle.
Gunmen kidnapped an engineer and his driver in Iligan, a largely Christian city, two months ago but freed them after a ransom was paid.
More than 40 people have been abducted since January in the Mindanao region, which is home to kidnap-for-ransom gangs and Moslem guerrillas fighting for an Islamic state.
